The '''Portland Timbers–Seattle Sounders rivalry''' is a [[Association football|soccer]] [[sports rivalry|rivalry]] between the [[Portland Timbers]] and [[Seattle Sounders FC]], both based in the [[Pacific Northwest]] region of the United States. The rivalry originated in the [[North American Soccer League (1968–84)|North American Soccer League]] of the 1970s, with both cities reviving expansion teams, and has carried into lower-level leagues, including the [[A-League (1995–2004)|A-League]] and [[USL First Division]]. The rivalry moved to [[Major League Soccer]], the top division of soccer in the United States, in 2011, where it has grown into one of the largest in American soccer.<ref name='KOMO News 2009-03-20'>{{cite news | title=Sounders FC get a rival – Portland awarded MLS franchise | date=March 20, 2009 | url =http://komonews.com/sports/content/sounders-fc-get-a-rival----portland-awarded-mls-franchise | work =KOMO News | access-date = July 22, 2016 }}</ref><ref name='Seattle Times 2003'>{{cite news | first=José | last=Romero| title=206 vs. 503: Soccer rivalry still simmers | date=August 8, 2003 | url =https://archive.seattletimes.com/archive/20030808/sounders08/206-vs-503-soccer-rivalry-still-simmers | work =The Seattle Times | access-date = April 11, 2009 }}</ref>

According to many players, the Seattle–Portland rivalry is one of the only true [[Local derby|derbies]] that is present in American men's soccer.<ref name='MLSnet.com News'>{{cite news|first=Andrew |last=Winner |title=Seattle-Portland rivalry remains intense |date=June 30, 2009 |url=http://web.mlsnet.com/news/mls_news.jsp?ymd=20090630&content_id=5617052&vkey=news_mls&fext=.jsp |work=MLSnet.com This rivalry "naturally translated into soccer" according to one fan.<ref name='Seattlest'/> The two cities also had a rivalry between the [[Seattle SuperSonics|SuperSonics]] and [[Portland Trail Blazers|Trail Blazers]] of the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]], known as the [[I-5 rivalry]], since both cities are connected by [[Interstate 5]].

==History==
===NASL era===
The [[Seattle Sounders (1974–83)|Seattle Sounders]] and [[Portland Timbers (1975–82)|Portland Timbers]] first played each other on May 2, 1975, in the Timbers' inaugural game. Seattle defeated Portland 1–0 in front of 8,131 at Portland Civic Stadium, now known as [[Providence Park]].<ref name="thenewstribune.com">{{cite web |url=http://www.thenewstribune.com/sports/soccer/story/796531.html |title=Seattle-Portland smoldering soccer rivalry gets new fire &#124; MORE TOP SPORTS |publisher=The News Tribune |access-date=May 31, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130204044230/http://www.thenewstribune.com/sports/soccer/story/796531.html |archive-date=February 4, 2013 |df=mdy-all }}</ref> The return match, played on July 26, 1975 saw Portland play spoils and defeat the hosts, Seattle 2–1, in front of a crowd of 27,310. A month later, Portland knocks Seattle out of the playoffs in front of a crowd of 31,000.<ref name='NASL Marketing, Inc 1977'>{{cite news | title=A NASL Rivalry, Portland vs. Seattle | year=1977 | url =http://soundercentral.com/museum/1977updates/Soccer%20Bowl%201977/seattle_portland_1977.htm | work =NASL Marketing, Inc. | access-date = April 12, 2009 }}</ref>

On June 30, 1979, Seattle defeated Portland 5–1 in the [[Kingdome]] in front of a season high 34,000 spectators. Until the 1980s, it would stand as the largest victory in the derby, and it is the largest victory by either side in the top tier of American soccer. In the 5–1 victory, Seattle's [[Derek Smethurst]] netted a hat trick.

At the end of the [[1982 North American Soccer League season]], the Portland Timbers franchise was forced to fold, as team expenditures outpaced club income. Consequently, the 1–0 Sounders victory over the Timbers on August 22, 1982 ended up being the final meeting between the two sides in the North American Soccer League. It would not be for nearly 30 years, in 2011, the two sides would meet against one another in the top flight of American soccer.<ref>{{cite web|title=Preview: Seattle Sounders FC vs. Portland Timbers|url=http://www.mlssoccer.com/matchcenter/2011-05-14-seattle-sounders-fc-vs-portland-timbers/preview|publisher=MLSSoccer.com|access-date=January 20, 2012|date=May 14, 2011}}</ref>

====NASL indoor====
In the [[1980–81 NASL Indoor season]] the two clubs faced one another for the first time in [[indoor soccer]]. On November 21, 1980 in front of 7,885 at Portland's Memorial Coliseum (now called [[Veterans Memorial Coliseum (Portland, Oregon)|Veterans Memorial Coliseum]]), the Timbers won, 6–4.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/576018987/?terms=Timbers%20Sounders&match=1|title=Timbers beat Sounders indoors|work=Longview Daily News (Longview, WA)|date=November 22, 1980|via=newspapers.com|page=D2|access-date=December 5, 2020}}</ref> The Sounders would claim victory in the next four meetings. Portland won the final three rivalry matches of [[1981–82 NASL Indoor season|1981–82 indoor]], including the teams' last-ever indoor match-up, 6–4, on the strength of [[Dale Mitchell (soccer)|Dale Mitchell]]'s hat trick on February 5, 1982.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/493664457/?terms=Sounders%20Timbers&match=1|title=Michell's hat-trick deadens Sounders|work=Vancouver Sun|date=February 6, 1982|via=newspapers.com|page=B2|access-date=December 5, 2020}}</ref>

===WSL/WSA era===

At the end of the 1983 NASL season, the original Seattle Sounders franchise terminated, with the league itself ceasing operations ahead of the 1985 season. In 1984, a [[Western Soccer Alliance]] franchise was granted to the Seattle area for a soccer club in the area that was branded as the [[Seattle Storm (soccer)|Seattle Storm]], and went under the F.C. Seattle moniker for a while.<ref>[http://goalwa.wordpress.com/museum/FCupdates/1984/gabriel_1984_seattle_fc.htm]{{dead link|date=May 2013}}</ref> The following year, a WSA franchise was also granted to the Portland area, where the rivalry continued through the late 1980s into the early 1990s.

===USL===
[[File:Emerald City Supporters Take 'Em All.jpg|thumb|Sounders' fans in Seattle during a match against Portland in 2008]]
After an 11-year hiatus, the rivalry continued in 2001, when the newly incarnated [[Portland Timbers (2001–10)|Portland Timbers]] hosted the [[Seattle Sounders (1994–2008)|Seattle Sounders]] on May 11, 2001 at the same stadium where the rivalry began, which was now known as PGE Park. In front of a crowd of nearly 12,300, the hosts walked away with a 2–0 victory.

July 21, 2001, former [[United States men's national soccer team|U.S. National Team]] player, [[Brian Ching]], would score the only goal in a 1–0 Sounders victory over the Timbers, as over 11,000 would be in attendance in Portland.

Ahead of the 2004 season, supporters of both the Sounders, Timbers, and their rival up the I-5 corridor, the [[Vancouver Whitecaps (1986–2010)|Vancouver Whitecaps]], created the [[Cascadia Cup]] which would be given to the supporters whose team had a stronger record against the two sides. The first formal Cascadia Cup match between the two resulted in a Timbers victory, defeating the Sounders 2–0 on May 1, 2004. During the four regular-season meetings during that season, the Sounders lost thrice and had one victory over Portland. However, in the 2004 USL First Division Playoffs, their first playoff meeting since 1975, the Sounders won 3–2 on aggregate over Portland, posting a 2–0 home victory in the second leg.

On September 18, 2005, Seattle knocked Portland out of the playoffs for a second straight year, as the Sounders defeated the Timbers 2–0 in Seattle.

In Seattle, the Sounders defeated the Timbers 3–1 on July 22, 2006, in a hotly contested match that accumulated eight yellow cards and one red.

On May 10, 2008, in front of over 10,000 at Qwest Field (now [[Lumen Field]]), Seattle and Portland played out a 0–0 draw in the final match the two teams would play each other in Seattle in the [[USL-1]]. On August 7, 2008, the Timbers and Sounders played each other for a final time in the Division 2 league, [[USL-1]].  Seattle defeated Portland 1–0 on the historic night,<ref name='Portland Tribune 2008'>{{cite news | first=Tony | last=Schick| title=Final Timbers-Sounders league match gets all fouled up| date=August 11, 2008 | url =http://www.portlandtribune.com/sports/story.php?story_id=121817501316511200 | archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20110608043346/http://www.portlandtribune.com/sports/story.php?story_id=121817501316511200 | url-status =dead | archive-date =June 8, 2011 | work =Portland Tribune | access-date = April 17, 2009 }}</ref> in front of a rambunctious 12,332 fans. The high-intensity match also included a total of six cards handed out and one ejection.

===MLS era===

On July 1, 2009, Seattle eliminated Portland 2–1 before a sold-out PGE Park crowd in the [[2009 Lamar Hunt U.S. Open Cup|U.S. Open Cup]]. [[Roger Levesque]] — a player Portland fans have had a particular dislike for — scored Seattle's first goal within the opening minute.<ref name="Seattle Times 2010-03-10"/><ref name="oregonlive.com">{{cite news| url=http://www.oregonlive.com/timbers/index.ssf/2009/06/timberssounders_matchup_a_figh.html | work=The Oregonian | title=Timbers-Sounders matchup: a 'fight for every ball' | date=June 29, 2009}}</ref> Levesque completed a [[goal celebration]], in which he stood still at the top of the Timbers penalty area while [[Nate Jaqua]] pretended to chop him down like a tree, ending with Levesque falling flat on his back.<ref name="Vondersmith">{{cite news|url=http://www.portlandtribune.com/sports/story.php?story_id=124651321242093100 |title=Nemesis Levesque's early goal sparks Seattle in 2-1 win over Portland |first=Jason |last=Vondersmith |work=Portland Tribune |date=July 1, 2009 |access-date=May 31, 2011}}{{dead link|date=May 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

A cold and rainy night on March 11, 2010, Portland defeated Seattle 1–0 in a preseason community shield charity match. The crowd of 18,606 in attendance that night at Qwest Field is one of the largest crowds to attend a preseason game between two [[Soccer in the United States|U.S.]] teams in American soccer history.

In hoping to stoke the rivalry for the future [[2011 Major League Soccer season]] — when the Timbers would be joining the Sounders in MLS &mdash; Portland unveiled a [[billboard]] displaying a Timbers crest and the words ''Portland, Oregon'' and ''Soccer City USA'' less than a mile from Qwest Field in Seattle.<ref name="Arnold">{{cite news |title=Timbers raise stakes in rivalry with Seattle |first=Geoffrey C. |last=Arnold |newspaper=The Oregonian |location=Portland |date=September 9, 2010 |url=http://www.oregonlive.com/timbers/index.ssf/2010/09/timbers_raise_stakes_in_rivalr.html |access-date=September 10, 2010 }}</ref> The billboard was broadcast to a nationwide audience on [[ESPN2]] during halftime of the Sounders home match versus [[Real Salt Lake]] that evening.<ref name="ReferenceA">{{Cite episode |title=Seattle Sounders FC vs. Real Salt Lake |series=MLS Primetime Thursday |series-link=MLS Primetime Thursday |network=ESPN2 |airdate=2010-09-09}}</ref>

In March 2011, the Timbers defeated the Sounders 2–0 in the preseason Cascadia Summit, a round robin game event involving the two teams and their Canadian rival, [[Vancouver Whitecaps FC]]. In their first match as both MLS sides, and the first time since 1982 the two played in the top division of American soccer the Timbers and the Sounders battled to a draw at a rain-soaked [[Qwest Field]] in front of 36,593 in the highly anticipated MLS debut of the three-way Cascadia Cup. This was a stadium record crowd to see a regular season MLS match, and included more than 500 traveling Portland fans. The return match, on July 10, 2011 saw Seattle earn a 3–2 road victory.

On October 7, 2012, Seattle hosted Portland at CenturyLink Field in front of 66,452 people, the second-largest stand-alone crowd in MLS history. The Timbers had their second chance of the year to clinch their first Cascadia Cup contested by all three sides, but lost 3–0 to the host Sounders.<ref name="Mayers">{{cite news|url=http://old.seattletimes.com/html/sounders/2019372636_sounders08.html |title=Nemesis Sounders don't disappoint record crowd, beating Portland 3-0|first=Joshua |last=Mayers |work=Seattle Times |date=October 7, 2012 |access-date=October 8, 2012}}</ref>

In the fourth round of the [[2015 U.S. Open Cup]], the Sounders hosted the Timbers at the [[Starfire Sports Complex]] in [[Tukwila, Washington]]. Seattle, the defending champions of the Open Cup, lost 3–1 and ended the match with only six players after three were sent off by the referee with red cards and [[Obafemi Martins]] was injured after all three substitutions had been used. The final red card was given to [[Clint Dempsey]] for tearing up the notebook of referee Daniel Radford, for which he was suspended an additional three Open Cup matches.<ref>{{cite news |last=Pentz |first=Matt |date=June 16, 2015 |title=Clint Dempsey, Sounders frustrated by refs in 3-1 U.S. Open Cup loss vs. Portland |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/sounders/sounders-ousted-from-us-open-cup-by-portland-3-1/ |work=The Seattle Times |access-date=May 30, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Williams |first=Bob |date=June 19, 2015 |title=Clint Dempsey three-match ban for ripping up referee's notebook opens up can of worms |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/11687946/Clint-Dempsey-three-match-ban-for-ripping-up-referees-notebook-opens-up-can-of-worms.html |work=[[The Daily Telegraph|The Telegraph]] |access-date=May 30, 2019}}</ref> The match was later nicknamed the "Red Card Wedding" by fans, a reference to an [[The Rains of Castamere|episode]] of the television series ''[[Game of Thrones]]'' with a "red wedding".<ref>{{cite news |last=Farley |first=Richard |date=August 26, 2016 |title=The five most epic Seattle Sounders-Portland Timbers clashes of the MLS era |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/us/features/five-epic-seattle-sounders-portland-timbers-games-mls-us-open-cup-video?page=0%2C2 |work=Four Four Two |access-date=May 30, 2019}}</ref>

From 2015 through 2021, either Portland or Seattle represented the MLS Western Conference in the [[MLS Cup]] title game. Seattle won two titles in four appearances, while Portland won one in three; the Timbers also won the 2020 [[MLS is Back Tournament]], held during the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Pentz |first=Matt |date=December 9, 2021 |title=Cascadian reign: How the Portland Timbers and Seattle Sounders have dominated MLS' Western Conference |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3007710/2021/12/09/cascadian-reign-how-the-portland-timbers-and-seattle-sounders-have-dominated-mls-western-conference/ |work=[[The Athletic]] |url-access=subscription |access-date=May 11, 2023}}</ref> From 2018 to 2022, the home team won only one of eleven rivalry matches played during the MLS regular season.<ref>{{cite news |last=Oshan |first=Jeremiah |date=July 8, 2022 |title=Lately, Sounders-Timbers rivalry has been defined by home-field disadvantage |url=https://www.sounderatheart.com/2022/7/8/23199229/seattle-sounders-portland-timbers-rivalry-home-field-disadvantage |work=Sounder At Heart |accessdate=May 11, 2023}}</ref> An August 2021 match at Providence Park ended in a 6–2 Sounders victory, the largest margin in the rivalry's history and the most goals conceded by the Timbers in any league competition.<ref>{{cite news |last=Murray |first=Caitlin |date=August 15, 2021 |title=Portland Timbers humiliated by Seattle Sounders in historic 6-2 loss despite Sebastian Blanco's return as starter |url=https://www.oregonlive.com/timbers/2021/08/portland-timbers-embarrassed-by-seattle-sounders-in-wild-derby-despite-sebastian-blancos-return-as-starter.html |work=The Oregonian |accessdate=May 11, 2023}}</ref> From May 2017 to October 2025, Portland was unbeaten in the 10 regular season away games (5 wins, 5 draws) played at Lumen Field in Seattle.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-10-19 |title=Timbers claim Cascadia Cup trophy after battling Sounders to 1-1 draw |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/sounders/timbers-claim-cascadia-cup-trophy-after-battling-sounders-to-1-1-draw/ |access-date=2024-11-05 |website=The Seattle Times |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Evans |first=Jayda |date=October 4, 2025 |title=Seattle Sounders earn 1st home win over rival Portland Timbers in 8 years |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/sounders/seattle-sounders-earn-1st-home-win-over-rival-portland-timbers-in-8-years/ |work=The Seattle Times |accessdate=October 7, 2025}}</ref>

On August 29, 2021, the Sounders and [[OL Reign]] hosted a men's–women's [[doubleheader (television)|doubleheader]] with their respective opponents from Portland (the Timbers and [[Portland Thorns FC|Thorns]]). The women's match, a 2–1 Reign victory, set a [[National Women's Soccer League]] attendance record, with 27,248 spectators, and was followed by 45,737 for the Sounders' 2–0 loss to the Timbers.<ref>{{cite news |last=Evans |first=Jayda |date=August 29, 2021 |title=Sounders get close, but not in the back of the net in loss to rival Timbers |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/sounders/sounders-get-close-but-not-in-the-back-of-the-net-in-loss-to-rival-timbers/ |work=The Seattle Times |accessdate=May 11, 2023}}</ref> A similar doubleheader was played on June 3, 2023, with 42,054 spectators reported for the Sounders match.<ref>{{cite news |last=Evans |first=Jayda |date=June 3, 2023 |title=Sounders kick off soccer doubleheader with goalless draw with Timbers |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/sounders/sounders-kickoff-soccer-doubleheader-with-goalless-draw-with-timbers/ |work=The Seattle Times |accessdate=October 7, 2025}}</ref>

==Supporter groups==
[[File:TA2009.JPG|thumb|right|The Timbers' Army, pictured in 2009]]
A bitter rivalry between the teams' supporter groups exists. The Portland Timbers are supported by the [[Timbers Army]], and Seattle Sounders by the [[Emerald City Supporters]]. The spirited groups have always shown a deep amount of resentment toward each other throughout the years.<ref name='Seattlest'>{{cite news | title=A Guide to hating the Portland Timbers | date=May 4, 2007 | url =http://seattlest.com/2007/05/04/a_guide_to_hating_the_portland_timbers.php| work =Seattlest | access-date = April 16, 2009 }}</ref><ref name="Portland Timbers fans take rivalry with Sounders FC to another level">{{cite news | url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/sounders/portland-timbers-fans-take-rivalry-with-sounders-fc-to-another-level/ | title=Portland Timbers fans take rivalry with Sounders FC to another level | publisher=The Seattle Times | first=José Miguel | last=Romero | date=June 30, 2009 | archive-date=2009-07-03 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090703061002/http://seattletimes.nwsource.com/html/sounders/2009399549_sounders30.html | url-access=limited | url-status=live | access-date=June 30, 2009}}</ref> With the proximity of the two cities, traveling fans of both sides witness hostile environments while visiting the opposing stadium. A rare moment of violence broke out in March 2010 after a preseason Timbers win in Seattle, when, three Sounders fans (who were supposedly not associated with any Sounders supporters group) assaulted a Timbers fan, choking and dragging him with his team scarf.<ref>{{cite news|last=Clarridge|first=Christine|title=Seattle soccer hooligans choke Timbers fan with scarf|url=http://seattletimes.nwsource.com/html/theblotter/2011367604_seattle_soccer_hooligans_choke.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100322191238/http://seattletimes.nwsource.com/html/theblotter/2011367604_seattle_soccer_hooligans_choke.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 22, 2010|publisher=Seattle Times|access-date=May 12, 2011|date=March 17, 2010}}</ref>[[File:Emerald City Supporter's tifo at the Sounders FC v. Timbers FC..jpg|thumb|Emerald City Supporter's "Build a Bonfire" [[tifo]] at the Sounders FC v. Timbers FC in 2013.]]

On March 20, 2009, at the Portland MLS expansion rally, League Commissioner [[Don Garber]] mentioned what a great region the [[Pacific Northwest]] is for soccer, and gave an example by the success of the new MLS team [[Seattle Sounders FC]].  However, his comment was met with heavy boos and jeers coming from the Timbers Army surrounding him.  Portland mayor, [[Sam Adams (Oregon politician)|Sam Adams]], then offered a challenge to the Seattle mayor for when the Timbers and Sounders meet in 2011.<ref name='The Oregonian'>{{cite news | first=Jerry | last=Ulmer| title=Timbers Army enlists to cheer MLS team| date=March 20, 2009 | url =http://www.oregonlive.com/timbers/index.ssf/2009/03/timbers_army_enlists_to_cheer.html| work =The Oregonian | access-date = April 17, 2009 }}</ref>

==Players and transfers==
A large portion of the Sounders-Timbers rivalry can be seen on the soccer field itself. Before Seattle made the jump to MLS, many on-field rivalries between the players existed. As the years progressed, this would only enhance the level of competition and intensify the matches.  An example of this was the notable rivalry between Timbers defender [[Scot Thompson]] and Sounders striker [[Roger Levesque]]. Levesque played in Seattle from 2006 to 2012, while Thompson played in Portland from 2004 to 2010.

Another reason the rivalry intensified was the transfer of star players between the two teams.  While many players transferred to the other rival city from when the Timbers resumed play in 2001, the most memorable was the signing of Portland's all time assist leader, and fan favorite [[Hugo Alcaraz-Cuellar]]<ref name='Seattle Times'>{{cite news | first=Matt | last=Massey| title=Former nemesis now a Sounder| date=April 12, 2007 | url =https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/sounders/former-nemesis-now-a-sounder/| work =Seattle Times | archive-date=2007-05-15 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070515205803/http://seattletimes.nwsource.com/html/soccer/2003663004_sounders12.html | url-access=limited | url-status=live | access-date = April 18, 2009 }}</ref> to Seattle in 2007.  That same season, Seattle star [[Andrew Gregor]] signed with Portland, thus creating tensions on the field, as the players became familiar with each other. While playing for the Sounders in 2003, Gregor had said "A lot of the guys, we know each other from years back, and we don't get along and stuff. It's always exciting."<ref name='Seattle Times 2003'/>

NASL and USL matches between the teams were intense and more physical than those of other teams in the leagues. Former Sounders head coach [[Sigi Schmid]] said in 2010 that Seattle, Portland, and Vancouver playing in the same league again will be "something that's going to be one of the key features of MLS".<ref name="Seattle Times 2010-03-10"/> The first of these was Seattle fan favorite [[Mike Fucito]] who came to Portland via the [[Montreal Impact (MLS)|Montreal Impact]] on April 20, 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.soccerbyives.net/soccer_by_ives/2012/04/timbers-trade-for-fucito.html |title=Timbers trade for Fucito |publisher=Soccer By Ives |date=April 20, 2012 |access-date=May 31, 2013}}</ref>

==Cups==
{{Further|Cascadia Cup}}
Between 2004 and 2008, the USL Seattle Sounders, Portland Timbers, and [[Vancouver Whitecaps (1986–2010)|Vancouver Whitecaps]] competed for the supporter-created [[Cascadia Cup]], to be awarded to the club that finished with the best record in each season series between the three teams. The Cascadia Cup was created to celebrate the strong rivalries between each of the three clubs. Seattle won the Cascadia Cup twice in these five years while Portland never won. Seattle was not involved in the 2009 or 2010 competitions, both of which were won by Portland. While both Seattle and Portland consider Vancouver to be a rival, both of the U.S. fanbases consider their rivalries with Vancouver more cordial than with one another.<ref name="Seattle Times 2010-03-10"/> In a 2011 story on the rivalry by ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' writer Grant Wahl, one Timbers Army member said about Vancouver fans, "It's hard to dislike them because they're so nice", and an Emerald City Supporters member added, "They're like the nice cousin that's never going to offend anyone at a party."<ref>{{cite news|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1186007/3/index.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110520025829/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1186007/3/index.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=May 20, 2011 |title=A Pacific Passion Play |first=Grant |last=Wahl |work=[[Sports Illustrated]] |page=3 |date=May 23, 2011 |access-date=May 31, 2011}}</ref> The [[Major League Soccer|MLS]] versions of the [[Vancouver Whitecaps FC|Whitecaps]], [[Seattle Sounders FC|Sounders]] and [[Portland Timbers|Timbers]] resumed contesting the Cascadia Cup, beginning with the 2011 season.
